Sam / team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the concrete telemetry/config asks so we can size the pilot and propose a Dedicated config. I kept this tight so ops can take action.

Summary from call
- Use case: real-time pricing assistant embedded in merchant dashboard (streaming responses to operator). Typical session = 1-6 messages, variable prompt size (templates + product list).
- Current expectation: baseline QPS ~ 8 qps steady, peak crest bursts up to 220 qps for ~30s during flash-pricing events. Median tokens/request ~ 420, p95 tokens/request ~ 1,900.
- Streaming: client expects token-by-token stream for partial responses; latency p95 for first byte target = 150ms.

Asks (what we need to size the pilot)
1) Sample payloads: attach 1 day of representative requests (JSON lines ideally). We can use this to simulate token mix and prefix duplication.
2) Minute-level QPS trace for the last 2 weeks (CSV with timestamp, qps, avg_tokens). Helps validate crest duration and recurrence.
3) Clarify concurrent session model: are concurrent open streams capped per operator or per tenant? If per operator, what's the typical concurrency?
4) Any hard p95 latency SLOs for completion vs first-byte? You mentioned "operator feel" targets — please confirm numeric SLOs.

What Redwood will do next
- Marissa will run an ingest + microbenchmark on our serving runtime using the sample payloads and produce a tokens/sec and GPU-concurrency estimate.
- Ben will propose three starter configs (economy / balanced / low-latency) with expected p95 first-byte and sustained tokens/sec per-instance.
- Monica will draft an SLA appendix for the pilot (routing, fallback to smaller model, monitoring windows).

Attachments: fastlane_qps_snapshot.csv (attached), sample_payloads.json (small subset attached).

Thanks — Rishi

High-level suggested starter configs based on patterns we saw on the call / attachments: 

1) Economy (cost-first)\- Model: open-encoder-7B-quant\- Suggested pool: 4 x 80GB A100 equiv GPUs (shared across tenants)\- Expected sustained tokens/sec per-GPU: ~1,600 (median payload)\- Expected p95 first-byte: ~260ms (steady), degrades during crest to ~550ms

2) Balanced (latency/cost)\- Model: redwood-lowlat-13B-q4\- Suggested pool: 6 x 80GB A100 equiv GPUs\- Expected sustained tokens/sec per-GPU: ~2,700\- Expected p95 first-byte: ~160ms (steady), ~300–400ms under crest with autoscaled burst slots

3) Low-latency (SLO-focused)\- Model: redwood-lowlat-33B-8bit\- Suggested pool: 8 x 80GB A100 equiv GPUs, dedicated for high-tier tenants\- Expected sustained tokens/sec per-GPU: ~4,200\- Expected p95 first-byte: ~110–140ms steady, ~180–240ms crest with graceful shedding

Operational notes
- Prefix/KV caching: if Fastlane can standardize a product-list key (or tiered cache key), we can often cut token re-encoding by 20–40% for repeated patterns. Please confirm prefix reuse.
- Streaming: for first-byte p95 targets, we recommend a low internal batching window (10–20ms) and opportunistic micro-batching only when queue depth > 8 to avoid head latency spikes.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller model for non-priority tenants during crest periods; circuit-breaker thresholds at 75% GPU capacity per-pool.

I'll assemble concrete instance counts and expected monthly unit costs once Marissa shares tokens/sec numbers from the replay.

— Ben
